summary: Weekly POC security sync. Reviewed SSO/SAML integration status, audit log retention and format, SOC2 docs requested, discussed data retention/PII concerns and KMS options for encryption. Decided next steps: Redwood to share SOC2 and SSO artifacts; customer to confirm retention window and network requirements for private connector. topics: SSO / SAML setup and test plan
Audit logs: events, retention, and access
Data retention / PII handling during pilot
Private deployment network and firewall requirements
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Nguyen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — SSO check-in, audit logs, retention, and any SOC2 artifacts you need.
[00:18] Laura Chen: Thanks Alex. yes we rode across the SSO config last night but we hit an issue with the redirect URI — it keeps showing an invalid audience error.
[00:32] Priya Joshi: okay, that's usually either the audience (aud) or the entity id mismatch — we can send an example SAML metadata and a checklist. did you set the entity id to the exact value from our metadata?
[00:46] Marcus Reed: we used the value from the portal but it's possible our IdP rewrites it, we have a proxy in front that does host header modifiers.
[01:00] Alex Nguyen: that proxy detail is important — it can break the SAML assertion. Priya will share a sample and a debug list — also we'll include steps for enabling debug-level SAML logs on our side.
[01:16] Priya Joshi: yes, I'll add the specific entries to look for — NameID format, audience, and the signature validation. and include a note about clock skew — we sometimes see failed assertions when clocks are off by more than 2 minutes.
[01:34] Jamal Ortiz: on retention — legal asked us to keep logs for 365 days for auditability, but product needs only 90 days for the pilot to reduce storage. is there a way to do tiered retention or archive?
[01:50] Alex Nguyen: we support configurable retention per environment; for the hosted pilot we can keep 90 days hot and archive/export to S3 or your blob for longer term. but for Private deployment we can match whatever policy you have.
[02:06] Laura Chen: important that audit logs include user identity, request ID, model version, and tokenization metadata — basically enough to repro a request for an investigation. do you have a schema sample?
[02:22] Priya Joshi: yes, we'll send a sample audit log schema — it'll include timestamp, user_id, request_id, model, prompt_id, tokens_in/tokens_out (approx), response hash. note: some fields may be pseudonymized by default depending on data retention settings.
[02:40] Marcus Reed: what about PII? we can't have raw customer data persisted longer than 30 days in some jurisdictions. how do you handle redaction or masking during the pilot?
[02:52] Alex Nguyen: good question. for hosted mode we have redaction options and we can set hooks to drop or mask PII before persisting. for Dedicated/Private deployments you control storage and can run server-side redaction. we'll need to know which fields you consider PII so we can add to the pipeline.
[03:10] Laura Chen: we'll share the privacy spec — also need to see encryption details. is KMS supported? can we bring our own key?
[03:20] Priya Joshi: yes, we support customer-managed keys (bring your own KMS/HSM) for Private and Dedicated. for hosted we offer envelope encryption and can integrate with your KMS via federated access in some enterprise agreements.
[03:36] Jamal Ortiz: any SOC2 docs? legal is asking for SOC2 Type II and recent pen test results.
[03:44] Alex Nguyen: we'll share our SOC2 Type II report and the executive summary of the latest third-party pen test. I'll upload those to the shared folder after the call.
[03:56] Laura Chen: do you have an SLA around data access logs and auditability? we need to show auditors that logs are immutable for a period.
[04:06] Priya Joshi: we append and version logs and support export to your immutable storage. for stricter requirements we recommend Private deployment where your infra enforces immutability.
[04:18] Marcus Reed: for the private connector, our network ops will need firewall rules and egress allowances — can you share the IP ranges and ports?
[04:28] Alex Nguyen: yes we'll provide a network requirements doc with CIDR ranges and port list. note that for dynamic scaling some ranges may be added, we'll include guidance for allowing our managed IP pool.
[04:40] Laura Chen: regarding audit logs format, can you show a sample line?
[04:45] Priya Joshi: sure — sample: { timestamp: 2026-06-16T17:24:10Z, user_id: "u-1234", request_id: "r-9876", model: "rw-open-13b-v1", prompt_hash: "abc123", tokens_in: 78, tokens_out: 412 } — the transcription may flatten some fields but we'll send the JSON schema.
[05:10] Jamal Ortiz: minor transcription note — sometimes your product names show up differently in our docs, we've seen rw-open vs redwood-open which confuses stakeholders.
[05:20] Alex Nguyen: thanks, good callout — we'll standardize naming in the artifacts we send.
[05:28] Laura Chen: one more on SSO — do you support SCIM for provisioning? we want automatic user sync.
[05:36] Priya Joshi: yes SCIM is supported for Enterprise; we can enable it for the pilot if you want to test provisioning flows.
[05:44] Marcus Reed: timeline — we want SSO test next Tuesday, can we do that?
[05:50] Alex Nguyen: yes, let's tentatively schedule on Tuesday the 23rd for an SSO test window. Priya will circulate available times.
[05:58] Laura Chen: ok and for the audit logs, after you send the schema we'll run it against our SIEM mapping and come back with any gaps.
[06:06] Priya Joshi: sounds good. Alex — I'll attach the SAML sample and the debug checklist and also include a sample audit log JSON.
[06:16] Alex Nguyen: perfect. Recap: Redwood will share SOC2 and pen-test summary, Priya sends SAML metadata + audit schema, Marcus will provide network requirements, Laura confirms retention window. Next call / SSO test scheduled for 2026-06-23.
[06:34] Jamal Ortiz: thanks everyone.
[06:36] Alex Nguyen: thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[06:39] (meeting ends)
